newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan seeks 20% electricity rate cut by 2001 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan seeks 20% electricity rate cut by 2001 - paper.

text.p: Japan's Trade Ministry and the electric power industry aim to cut electricity rates by about 20 percent from current levels by 2001 by reducing capital investment in the sector, a business daily said on Tuesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said large investment in construction of power plants had made Japan's electricity rates high compared with those of other developed countries.

The ministry and the industry will seek to cut rates through increasing use of existing plants and buying electricity from non-utility firms, the paper said. If the rates cannot be cut through such steps, they may consider drastically changing operations of power firms which currently generate and provide electricity, it said.
The change could lead to separation of power generating and power providing businesses to be handled by different companies, it said.
The ministry and electric power companies were not immediately available for comment on the report.
